chat.answerExcerpt: Sunshine drives the hydrologic cycle by adding solar energy to seawater, turning liquid water into vapor that rises into the sky. That vapor cools and condenses into droplets, forming clouds. Gravity later brings it back as storms. Some of the rain runs downhill, and some soaks underground, refilling hidden reservoirs in porous rock.
